lineage: L7 FSI benchmark. Fluid-structure interaction: Newtonian fluid + elastic solid.

governance_compliance.article_XXIV: FSI formula from FEBio source (FEFluid.cpp, FENewtonianFluid.cpp)
governance_compliance.CE_029: Analytical BCs must match solver BCs

febio_fsi_from_source.pressure_equation: p = k * (1 - 1/J) for linear elastic fluid (k = bulk modulus)
febio_fsi_from_source.fsi_coupling: FEBio uses FEBiphasicFSI / FEFluidFSIDomain3D for coupled fluid-solid solve. Interface traction = fluid stress + solid stress at boundary.

field_1_geometry.shape: Channel flow past elastic obstruction (2D extruded to 3D)
field_1_geometry.fluid_domain: Channel 4x1x1, inlet at x=0, outlet at x=4
field_1_geometry.solid_domain: Elastic block 0.5x0.5x1 at center of channel (obstruction)
field_1_geometry.fsi_interface: Surface between fluid and solid domains

field_2_material.fluid: Newtonian: mu=0.01 Pa·s (water-like), rho=1.0, k=1e6 (nearly incompressible)
field_2_material.solid: incomp neo-Hookean (split): G=0.3846, k=0.8333 (same as L3)

field_4_loading.inlet: Prescribed velocity v_x = 0.1 at x=0 (Poiseuille profile)
field_4_loading.walls: No-slip at y=0, y=1, z=0, z=1

field_5_observable.primary: Solid displacement at obstruction center (u_x, u_y, u_z)
field_5_observable.tertiary: Maximum von Mises stress in solid

field_6_analytical.approach: For low Reynolds number (Stokes flow) past a small obstruction, analytical solutions exist for drag force and pressure drop. The solid deformation can be computed from the fluid drag force using the L3 elastic model.
field_6_analytical.simplification: For the benchmark, use a simpler problem: steady Stokes flow in a channel (no obstruction) to validate fluid solver, then add elastic wall (FSI) for the coupled case.
field_6_analytical.stokes_pressure_drop: delta_p = 12 * mu * U * L / h^2 for plane Poiseuille flow (h=channel height, L=length, U=mean velocity)

field_9_state_vars: fluid velocity, fluid pressure, solid displacement, FSI interface traction
key_challenge: FSI is the most complex physics so far. Requires: (1) fluid solver (Navier-Stokes), (2) solid solver (hyperelasticity), (3) FSI coupling at interface (traction equilibrium). FEBio has FEBioFluid module; SfePy has Navier-Stokes terms but no native FSI coupling.
